_comment: The WHO SMART Base layer, staged as a top-level directory ahead of becoming its own repository — the same path `who-iris`, `smart-trust` and `smart-immunizations` are already on. The owner settled the location 2026-09-22: "same as other smart-* now in corpus... we are migrating. want KG assets here, can break apart later. OK to reference smart-* github sources (e.g markdown) per the smart-* harnessing insutrctiots. needs smart-base harness". Bean `nsbb` had already called for this harness from the other direction — it rules that a per-IG harness should not exist because it adds no new functionality, and that the DAK/IG pipeline belongs in an IG base under a NEW `smart-base` harness. This is that harness. It holds KG ASSETS first — the ingested WHO digital-health corpus, the methodologies read out of it, and the voices derived from it — and takes no position on the pipeline layering, which is `nsbb`'s to settle. THE UPSTREAM TOOLCHAIN IS NOT VENDORED HERE: `WorldHealthOrganization/smart-base` stays the authoritative home of the ~54 Python scripts, and `smart-base-tools` states why — a copy here would be a second, drifting toolchain.

_title_comment: The HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs. `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames, `needs` edges and `declaredBy` resolve against; `title` is what a reader sees and nothing resolves against it. Bean `t3n8`.
title: SMART Base
description: The WHO SMART Guidelines base layer — the ingested WHO digital-health corpus, the methodologies read out of it, and the editorial voices derived from it.

directories.description: The reader-facing pages, and the landing page `/smart-base/` serves. Generated by `smart-base:pages` (`fhir-harness/scripts/gen-ig-pages.ts --summary`) from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` plus this declaration: the index page opens with this instance's own description and every declared graph with its viewer (the `harness_details.html` include over `site.data.harness`), then the artefact index. WHY IT EXISTS: before it, smart-base declared no renderable graph, so `/smart-base/` published nothing and the navbar tile fell back to the library viewer -- `harness-tiles.ts` reported that as a finding. Owner, 2026-10-01 (#1767): "smart-base/ needs a landing page". NOTHING HERE IS AUTHORED; `smart-base:pages:check` is the gate. The banner names THIS IG (`smart.who.int.base`) from the index, not the IG the chrome was ingested from, and draws no status watermark because the chrome's status is smart-trust's (bean `bamf`).
directories._comment_composed: Rendered THROUGH just-the-docs, as smart-trust's are -- the same reasoning, recorded on `smart-trust-docs`.

directories.description: L1 source content: one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested WHO publication, holding `sections/*.md` and `structure.json`. Every knowledge-graph reference to one of these sources resolves through here, never to a loose path or a bare URL — which is the whole reason the bytes could not stay in `uploads/`. The corpus-grep checklist searches `library/` ONLY, so a publication left in the incoming queue does not merely go unread: it makes a clean grep mean "nobody has done this" while the source sits right there. The id is `library`, the CONVENTIONAL one, so this entry OVERRIDES the default rather than joining it — overrides match on id and never on path, and a distinct id at the same path yields two entries for one directory that every fan-out consumer then scans twice.

Methodologies adopted from the WHO digital-health corpus in `library/` -- somebody else's work, adopted whole, never a house process with a citation bolted on. `diig.md` is the first. Declared in the commit that created its content rather than ahead of it: a declared-but-absent directory is the `dh4f` defect, where every consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. `skip` rather than `reproduce` because a downstream instance inherits the METHOD by depending on this layer, not by copying the directory.

The executable half of this layer's methodologies -- `diig-investment-path.bpmn` renders DIIG's own nine chapters as a process with its two progress checks as gateways. A SEPARATE declaration from `methodologies/` even though it nests inside it, because `processes` and `methodology` are different graph kinds and a directory entry names one graph: the prose node says what the method IS, the diagram says how it RUNS. Bean `x4v4` raised whether `methodologies/` is a graph or a folder; this follows the shape already on main, where `methodology-crdm-processes` is declared beside `methodologies/` rather than inferred from it. Issue #877, bean `qnvy`.

The BPMN this layer OWNS as a house process, as against `methodologies/processes/`, which holds the executable half of a methodology adopted whole from the corpus. `l2-dak-authoring.bpmn` is the first: moved here from cat-harness/processes/ on 2026-10-01 by owner ruling (issue #1772 item 3), because placement PR1 had moved its `l2-dak-authoring` skill into `skills/content/authoring-who-smart-guidelines/` and the three activities naming it no longer resolved from cat-harness, which cannot reach this layer. Here the skill sits beside the diagram; the remaining refs (`content-plan`, `todo-manager`, `bpmn-authoring`, `dmn-authoring`, `content-review`, `content-validate`, `terminology-management`) point down, through `fhir-harness`. A TOP-LEVEL directory rather than a second file in `methodologies/processes/`, for the reason `folio-assistant-core-processes` gives: that nested shape is a baselined `check:layout-norms` exception, and a house process is not a methodology read out of `library/`. Declared WITH its file in one commit, per bean `dh4f`.

The published IG's artefact index, reconstructed by `ingest:ig` from smart.who.int.base v0.3.0 (FHIR 4.0.1). 225 artefacts known, 47 materialized -- the DAK API surface, whose JSON Schemas and OpenAPI have no other home, against resource JSON that does. `dak/` sits INSIDE this directory rather than beside it, so one entry covers both the index and the bytes it points at; a sibling would be an undeclared directory holding the very bytes the index claims to have, which is the `dh4f` shape. NOTHING HERE IS AUTHORED: `ingest:ig:check` re-derives it and a hand-edit is a defect the next check either overwrites or reports. The four CDHI/CDSC ConceptMaps -- the v1-to-v2 crosswalks and the two hierarchy maps -- are indexed `referenced`: the index says where they are and holds none of their rows. Materializing one is `materialize-remote.bpmn`, not a flag. Issue #877, bean `cpmo`. UNTIL plan Q4 (bean `rbz3`, 2026-10-02) IT ALSO HELD `chrome.json`; the chrome is the TEMPLATE's styling, so it now lives in `themes/` beside the template's theme, and ships with the harness. When it was here, it was a THIRD provenance in one directory rather than a second copy of an existing one: `index.json` is harvested from an IG's published output, `menu.json` (smart-trust's) is read from its `sushi-config.yaml`, and `chrome.json` is resolved from the `fhir.template` packages its `ig.ini` names -- `fhir.base.template` and `who.template.root`, separate repositories the IG merely depends on. An IG declares its appearance in NO file it owns, which is why the chrome could not be folded into either of the other two. It lives at smart-base so every WHO SMART IG (through `smart-ig`) inherits one answer instead of each re-copying it; `schemas/ig-chrome.ts` carries why the consumer NAMES this instance rather than walking `needs` to it, and the layering gap that forces it, which is `nsbb`'s.
directories.readOnlyBasis: Copies of upstream IG artefacts, and GENERATED -- `ingest-ig-artifacts.ts` rewrites this index, a person does not edit it. Read-only is about the second: a hand edit here silently changes what this repository claims upstream published, and `check:materialized-fixity` is what catches one that happened. Answered rather than left silent, because absent is NOT a declaration of writability -- a directory that has not answered has asserted nothing, which is why the verdict for silence is `undeclared` and never `false`.

directories.description: smart-base's Tool nodes. The owner, 2026-09-22: "things like dmn -> fhir questionnaire should be a tool. the skill/tools under smart-base should consolidate under the smart-base/tools/ directory under this repo", serving "want to slowly get smart-base back to a more conventional IG state w/o tooling". THIS REVERSES NOTHING THIS FILE'S HEADER SAYS: the header refuses to VENDOR the upstream Python, and a Tool node is a declaration -- what the capability consumes, what it produces, which skill it satisfies -- not a copy of a line of it. Declare here, execute upstream, until the execution moves too. The two Library strippers are deliberately NOT here: they are not DAK-shaped and belong to `fhir-harness` by the placement question in `smart-stack-layering`, and filing them here to tidy the list would be a step's own name overruling the layering rule.

What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 12 files across methodologies (1), scenarios (1), skills (1), tools (9). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. dependents: reproduce, because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it.

directories._comment: The WHO SMART IG template's web theme, DERIVED from the stylesheet the IG actually builds with. Bean `7h3u`, issue #1682, on the owner's 2026-09-30 ruling: theme it, keep the just-the-docs machinery, WHO's styling, and the nav on the LEFT rather than their top bar. THE SOURCE IS NOT THIS IG. `WorldHealthOrganization/smart-trust` carries no branding CSS at all; its `ig.ini` selects `#local-template`, whose package.json declares `base: who.template.root` -- and that is `WorldHealthOrganization/smart-ig-template`, whose `content/assets/css/who.css` is the branding. It is vendored under `upstream/` so the test reads a COMMITTED artefact rather than the network, and because `local-template` depends on `who.template.root#current`, which can re-skin under us at any time. CC0-1.0, stated by that package's own package.json, is what makes vendoring permitted. Moved from `smart-trust/themes/` in stage D of the smart-* separation (#1767, bean `kg83`): the theme is the TEMPLATE's, and smart-base is the harness every smart-* IG instantiates. Declared rather than left implicit because an undeclared directory is the `dh4f` defect: every declaration-driven consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it.
directories.description: The WHO SMART IG template's web theme, measured from `who.template.root`'s own `who.css` and pinned by commit. Colour and geometry only: the IG's top navbar is deliberately not reproduced, because the owner asked for the nav to stay on the LEFT (2026-09-30). `upstream/who.css` is the vendored source the tests re-read, CC0-1.0.
directories._dependents_comment: skip, not reproduce -- the same reasoning `who-iris-themes` carries. This entry says where THIS instance's theme lives; a dependent with no theme of its own needs no themes/ directory, and reproduce would ship an empty one downstream, which is the `dh4f` shape arriving by inheritance.

directories._comment: Document KINDS this harness contributes (stage D5 of the smart-* separation, #1767, bean qvxh): named structures of sections a document authored with smart-base follows. The owner's reframe: L1 and DAK are document kinds inside smart-base, not harness layers. dak.json is GENERATED from DAK_COMPONENTS by smart-base/scripts/gen-document-kinds.ts (gated by smart-base:document-kinds:check); l1.json and dth.json are authored from their sources once those are ingested (beans tyo0, 5blc).
directories.description: WHO SMART document kinds: the DAK (a fixed structure, the ten components) and, to follow, L1 (semi-fixed) and the Digital Transformation Handbook (an L1 subtype).

Findings about the WHO digital-health corpus in `library/` that are recorded for the owner rather than adopted: where sources disagree, each version kept as an alternative with its citation. `dth-term-alternatives.json` is authored (the one DIIG phase figure and its reproductions, approaches recorded as alternatives, and what "actor" means in the RA, SMART Guidelines and folio-assistant, with one proposal per layer); `dth-terms.md` is GENERATED from it and the DTH candidate list by `smart-base:dth-terms` (`smart-base/scripts/gen-dth-term-findings.ts`), and `smart-base:dth-terms:check` fails on a stale page or on a quote that no longer matches its source. A SEPARATE directory from `docs/` because `docs/` is wholly generated by `smart-base:pages`, whose check reports any other file there as an orphan. Owner, 2026-10-03 (#1984, bean `5blc`): "make a docs page under smart-base showing the glossary/terms differences findings".

directories._comment: smart-kg, PINNED rather than copied (owner 2026-10-02, #1767: 'subgraph in smart-base to help define l1 dth etc docs'; and 2026-09-23, bean wg7r: 'that is its own repo already'). One external-schema record naming the commit, and the class ids of smart-kg's L1 and L2 layers at that commit, DERIVED by smart-base/scripts/pin-smart-kg.ts so smart-base:document-kinds:check can resolve a section's `modelledBy` offline. Bean pebe.

_canonicalUrl_comment: smart-base's published base, as `sushi-config.yaml` declares it (`canonical: http://smart.who.int/base`). Added 2026-09-22 with `tools/`, because a Tool node's I/O type IRIs are minted against this at load and Zod refuses a relative one. It is READ from upstream rather than chosen here, so it is a fact about smart-base and not a decision about where this staging directory publishes.
_needs_comment: REPOINTED 2026-09-22 (issue #975) from `folio-assistant-core` to `fhir-harness`, per the owner's stack ruling. It read `folio-assistant-core` because it was staged (PR #881) BEFORE `fhir-harness` existed, and taking no position on the pipeline layering was that PR's explicit scope. `needs` governs the LAYER ORDER: `dependency-order.ts` topologically sorts on it and `harness-tiles.ts` builds the LHS navbar spine from it. It does NOT compose the skill or content overlay -- that is `dependencies.folioAssistant` in `<name>.config.json`, walked recursively by `resolveSkillDirs`, and the two are different mechanisms with different files. MEASURED 2026-09-22 rather than assumed, after this comment first claimed otherwise: with `needs` set correctly, `resolveSkillDirs` still returns each instance's OWN skills and nothing from the layer below. No `smart-*` instance declares config dependencies at all, so no overlay composes anywhere in this stack -- bean recorded, not fixed here.
